sections.heading: Glossary term: Molecule
sections.body: A molecule is a group of two or more atoms which are bound together by what are known as chemical bonds and carries zero net electric charge. In chemistry, molecules are limited to atoms bound together by covalent bonds, but in astronomy ionic compounds are sometimes referred to as "molecules". Molecules are present in conditions that range from the atmospheres of solar type and cooler stars and brown dwarfs; to the atmospheres, oceans, and icy regions of planets and moons; to icy material on comets and asteroids; as well as the colder parts of the interstellar medium. In order to form new stars it takes interstellar molecular clouds made mostly of hydrogen molecules (H2). A new star is formed as part of such a cloud contracts under its own gravity. Molecules can be detected in space because under the right circumstances, as they rotate or vibrate, they absorb and emit electromagnetic radiation in narrow wavelength regions, typically in the radio or infrared. These "molecular lines" form patterns that allow for the identification of a molecule.

sections.source_html:
Glossary term: Molecule

Description: A molecule is a group of two or more atoms which are bound together by what are known as chemical bonds and carries zero net electric charge. In chemistry, molecules are limited to atoms bound together by covalent bonds, but in astronomy ionic compounds are sometimes referred to as "molecules".

Molecules are present in conditions that range from the atmospheres of solar type and cooler stars and brown dwarfs; to the atmospheres, oceans, and icy regions of planets and moons; to icy material on comets and asteroids; as well as the colder parts of the interstellar medium. In order to form new stars it takes interstellar molecular clouds made mostly of hydrogen molecules (H2). A new star is formed as part of such a cloud contracts under its own gravity.

Molecules can be detected in space because under the right circumstances, as they rotate or vibrate, they absorb and emit electromagnetic radiation in narrow wavelength regions, typically in the radio or infrared. These "molecular lines" form patterns that allow for the identification of a molecule.

Related Terms:

  • Atom
  • Electromagnetic Radiation
  • Energy Level


See this term in other languages

Term and definition status: This term and its definition have been approved by a research astronomer and a teacher

The OAE Multilingual Glossary is a project of the IAU Office of Astronomy for Education (OAE) in collaboration with the IAU Office of Astronomy Outreach (OAO). The terms and definitions were chosen, written and reviewed by a collective effort from the OAE, the OAE Centers and Nodes, the OAE National Astronomy Education Coordinators (NAECs) and other volunteers. You can find a full list of credits here. All glossary terms and their definitions are released under a Creative Commons CC BY-4.0 license and should be credited to "IAU OAE".

If you notice a factual error in this glossary definition then please get in touch.
sections.body_ru: Молекула — это группа из двух или более атомов, связанных так называемыми химическими связями и имеющая нулевой суммарный электрический заряд. В химии молекулами называют только группы атомов, соединённых ковалентными связями, но в астрономии ионные соединения иногда называют «молекулами». Молекулы встречаются в самых разных условиях: в атмосферах звёзд солнечного типа, более холодных звёзд и коричневых карликов; в атмосферах, океанах и ледяных областях планет и спутников; в ледяном веществе комет и астероидов; а также в более холодных частях межзвёздной среды. Для образования новых звёзд требуются межзвёздные молекулярные облака, состоящие в основном из молекул водорода (H2). Новая звезда образуется, когда часть такого облака сжимается под действием собственной гравитации. Молекулы можно обнаружить в космосе, потому что при определённых условиях, когда они вращаются или колеблются, они поглощают и испускают электромагнитное излучение в узких областях длин волн, обычно в радио- или инфракрасном диапазоне. Эти «молекулярные линии» образуют спектральные картины, которые позволяют идентифицировать молекулу.
